title: Stop paying for error messages nobody reads

blocks.text: The warehouse scans forty thousand shipments an hour, and every scan goes through `ShipmentChecks` before a label is printed. A profile of the scanner shows most of the checker's time in `describe`, which formats every parcel of a shipment, and in building not-found errors, each with its stack trace. Yet fewer than one shipment in ten thousand lacks a carrier, and unknown ids are rarer still.

Finish `carrierOf` and `find` in `src/main/java/practice/ShipmentChecks.java`. A shipment without a carrier fails with a `NullPointerException` whose message is its description, and an unknown id with the exception `notFound` builds for it; the shipments and ids that pass must cost nothing extra. About two lines in total.

cases.says: a shipment with a carrier returns it; one without fails with a NullPointerException carrying its description
a known id returns its shipment; an unknown one throws the error built for it
checking shipments that have a carrier never formats a description
looking up ids that exist never builds the not-found error

origin.section: The JDK Takes a Supplier Where the Work May Not Be Needed

concepts: Objects.requireNonNull(obj, Supplier) and Optional.orElseThrow(Supplier) call the supplier only on the failing path, while the String overload builds its message on every call.
